summary: Iteration 9 — targeted backend regression of the Emergent File & Media Storage integration only (iterations 5/6/7 suites intentionally NOT rerun). New test file /app/backend/tests/test_iteration9_storage.py: 13 pytest tests, 13 PASSED (100%). Verified: (1) GET /api/health returns status/database healthy and storage='emergent'; (2) sanity logins for patient@/doctor1@/admin@careflow.demo + /api/auth/me; (3) POST /api/reports/upload as admin with a PDF returns storage_backend='emergent', storage_path 'careflow/reports/{patient_id}/{uuid}.pdf', NO file_id and no _id, file_size correct, visibility='private'; GET /api/reports/{id}/file returns 200 byte-identical bytes with Content-Type application/pdf; (4) PNG upload -> path ends .png and download returns byte-exact PNG with Content-Type image/png; (5) PATCH /api/reports/{id}/visibility -> 'patient_visible': target patient 200 byte-exact (and 404 before release), other patient (patient1@) 404, non-uploader doctor2@ 403, unauthenticated 401; (6) POST /api/patient-documents/upload as patient -> storage_backend='emergent', path 'careflow/patient-documents/{user_id}/...', status='pending_review'; GET /api/patient-documents/{id}/file: owner 200 byte-exact, other patient 404, doctor 403, admin 200 byte-exact; (7) legacy rows with file_id and no storage_path still stream 200 from private_uploads for the authorized admin (3 legacy reports checked); (8) two concurrent uploads produced two distinct storage_paths with byte-exact independent contents (no collision); (9) rejection paths intact — text/plain -> 400 on both upload endpoints, >10MB PDF -> 413. All Mongo rows created by this run (5 reports + 1 patient document) were deleted; verified 0 iter9 rows remain. No product code changed; backend logs show only the pre-existing benign passlib/bcrypt __about__ warning.

minor.issue: If storage_get() raises (Emergent storage outage, expired storage key beyond the single retry), the exception is swallowed and the endpoint returns 404 'no longer available'. A real backend/storage failure is indistinguishable from a deleted record — prefer 502/503 for transport failures so it is observable.

Synchronous `requests` calls executed inside async request handlers (including /api/health via storage_available()) block the event loop for the whole upload/download (timeouts 120s/60s). Under concurrency this serialises the server; consider httpx.AsyncClient or run_in_threadpool.
The whole body is read into memory (await file.read()) before the 10 MB check, so the 413 path still buffers arbitrarily large payloads. Use Content-Length pre-check or chunked read with early abort.
22 leftover TEST_/UITEST rows from iterations 5–7 still pollute the collection (plus orphaned blobs in backend/private_uploads). Pre-existing, not caused by this iteration; my own rows were removed.

action_items: Optional: distinguish storage transport failures (502/503) from missing records (404) in read_upload().
Optional: make Emergent storage calls non-blocking (async client or threadpool), and avoid calling storage_available() on every /api/health hit.
Optional housekeeping: purge the 22 leftover TEST_/UITEST patient_documents rows and orphaned private_uploads blobs.
critical_code_review_comments: save_upload correctly returns storage_backend+storage_path for Emergent and storage_backend+file_id for local, so legacy rows (file_id, no storage_backend) fall through to the disk branch — verified working for existing rows.
storage_put re-inits the storage key on 403/404 and retries once — good resilience for expired keys.
Blocking `requests` usage inside async endpoints is the main architectural concern of this integration.
server.py is now 420 dense lines with multi-statement one-liners; splitting routers (auth/reports/storage) would improve maintainability.
